subject: Staff briefing: hotspots & targeted asks — week of Dec 18
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>, maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Staff briefing: hotspots & targeted asks — week of Dec 18

Team — attaching a concise briefing for the week. This is intentionally short; key points below and asks at the end. Appendix and the OKR tracker are attached. Please flag any objections inline.

Top-level summary
- Wins: Dedicated launch warm-up completed for EU cluster (smoke tests green); Redwood Optimize pilot reduced mean token CPU by ~12% in internal benchmark.
- Hotspots (risks): Latency variance on long-context flows (p95 spikes with 16k sequences); SOC 2 evidence for log-retention still pending from external auditor.
- Primary asks: 1) Decision on temporary SLA extension for EU pilot (owner: Laura) by Mon 21st; 2) Approval to re-route a controlled subset of traffic to quantized model for A/B (owner: Markus) by EOD Tue 22nd; 3) Sign-off to share partial audit artifacts with SigmaAudit to unblock SOC 2 timeline (owner: Maya).

OKR check-ins (high level)
- Q3-Q4 Delivery OKR (Model Serving Reliability) — On track for throughput targets, behind on p95 latency target (current 450ms target, p95 at 550ms for long-context). Action: Markus to propose kernel fallback within 48 hours.
- Cost Efficiency OKR — Making progress via Optimize pilot; projected -8% net infra spend if rollout proceeds. Action: Finance needs one-slide summary for QBR (Vivek).
- Enterprise Expansion OKR — Two demos scheduled with Enterprise prospects; pre-sales asks noted below.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: p95 latency spikes may impact SLAs for early EU Dedicated customers. Mitigation: Canary fallback to 8-bit quantized variant, targeted limit of 5% traffic. Ops to instrument per-route tracing before rollout.
- Risk: SOC 2 evidence delay could push compliance sign-off into January. Mitigation: Provide SigmaAudit with redactable log samples; escalate procurement to request expedited review.

Targeted asks (owners & deadlines)
1) Laura — Approve temporary SLA amendment for EU pilot (Mon 2026-12-21 COB). Text for amendment included in appendix.
2) Markus — Confirm A/B routing plan + rollout guardrail (Tue 2026-12-22 EOD). Include expected perf delta and fallback criteria.
3) Maya — Authorize sharing of redactable logs with SigmaAudit and send vendor contact; also confirm internal evidence owner for retention policy (Wed 2026-12-23).
4) Vivek — Produce a one-slide cost-benefit summary for QBR (due Thu 2026-12-24).

Quick notes for QBR prep
- I'm keeping the appendix deliberately short — see drive links. If we get approvals on the three asks above, I'll assemble a 6-slide narrative for the leadership QBR by Friday.

Attachments: QBR_appendix_v1.pdf (1p), OKR_tracker.xlsx (summary tab).

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Staff Operations | Redwood Inference

Approved in principle. Olga — please include the temporary SLA amendment language in the QBR appendix that limits customer exposure and sets a hard rollback date (30 days), and add an explicit communications line for affected customers.

Markus — agree with per-route scoping for the quantized fallback; keep the impact window to under 5% of requests per route and include an automated rollback at 5% error or 2x p95 baseline.

Maya — proceed with the redaction-demo; procurement — please prioritize. Laura is looping in CS for customer comms draft (separate thread).

I'll review the one-slide cost summary once Vivek posts it. Thanks for the concise brief — keeps the QBR timeline realistic.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Chief Operating Officer | Redwood Inference
